To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) aptamer-based assays for the diagnosis and drug resistance monitoring of leishmaniasis are being developed; (2) aptamers that bind to parasite-specific molecules have been used to deliver cytotoxic molecules to parasites; (3) the development of aptamer-based therapeutics is being pursued; (4) aptamers are being used as biosynthetic tools to identify parasite-specific molecules and to study the molecular basis of parasite-host interaction.

(i) we have developed a new aptamer-based assay to identify and quantify parasite-specific molecules in biological samples; (ii) we have used the aptamer-based assay for the first time in clinical samples to detect and quantify parasite-specific antigens; (iii) we have identified a parasite-specific aptamer that binds to a parasite-specific protein; (iv) we have developed an aptamer-based assay that allows the detection of parasite-specific molecules in a clinical sample and (v) we have identified
aptamers can bind to parasite-derived molecules with a high affinity and specificity and that these aptamers are useful as biosynthetic tools to identify and purify parasite-specific molecules.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of aptamers as reagents in the field of parasitology.

the generation of parasite-specific aptamers, which are used as tools to investigate parasite biology, as biosynthetic agents for the production of parasite-derived molecules and as potential pharmaceuticals.

the development of novel parasite-specific aptamers for the purpose of generating biosynthetic reagent for the detection and characterization of parasites and parasite-derived molecules, and for the design of novel pharmaceuticals.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the number of parasite-specific aptamers is too limited to draw a clear picture of their potential.
the field of parasite-specific aptamers is still in its infancy.
the number of parasite-specific aptamers is still limited and that their potential for parasite diagnosis or treatment has not yet been fully realized.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the selection of aptamers against parasites and parasite molecules has been slow.
aptamers are versatile reagents for the analysis and manipulation of parasites.
parasite-specific aptamers are not yet widely used in the field.
The main takeaway from our work is that
aptamers can serve as a source for novel parasite-specific reagents that can be used for a wide range of applications in parasite biology and medicine.
aptamers have great potential as tools for the development of new drugs, diagnostics and vaccines against parasitic diseases.
aptamers can be used as biosynthetic agents to produce parasite-specific ligands that are not accessible by any other means.
